findings.title: RPCs are no longer rejected after Stop()
findings.body:
Stop() stores "service is stopping" / "service is stopped" in s.initErr (server.go:321, 339). Before this change every RPC began with s.Init(ctx), which returned that error, so calls after Stop failed. LifecycleHooks.Stop documents that storage calls may error after Stop (hooks.go:19). The diff removes that gate from Create (server.go:451), Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy (server.go:934-935), PutBlob and GetBlob, and nothing replaces it.

The effect: backend Stop cancels the poller (backend.go:119-121, poller exits on b.done at backend.go:575-578). Search consumes WatchWriteEvents (search.go:203-213), so a write accepted after Stop returns success to the client but never reaches the search index or the watchers. IsHealthy now reports the diagnostics result, so a stopping instance can keep reporting healthy.

Fix: keep a stopped check (for example s.initErr or a stopped flag) at the top of the RPCs that must refuse work after Stop, and at least in IsHealthy.

verification.reason: Stop still sets s.initErr to 'service is stopping'/'service is stopped' (server.go:321,339), but the diff removed the s.Init(ctx) gate from every RPC, and that gate was the only thing returning initErr to callers. RPCs now go through after Stop, even though hooks.go:19 says calls may error after Stop.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads b.cache without the lock that now guards its writes
findings.body:
TotalDocs ranges over b.cache (bleve.go:145-146) with no lock. The diff makes BuildIndex take cacheMu around the map write (bleve.go:137-139), so writers are locked and this reader is not. GetIndex (bleve.go:61-62) takes RLock, so the pattern exists in the same type.

There are two concurrent callers. BleveIndexMetrics.Collect calls TotalDocs on every Prometheus scrape (pkg/storage/unified/resource/bleve_index_metrics.go:96) while builds run from Search and the watch goroutine. The new call in init at pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 runs after the watch goroutine has been started (search.go:207-213), so a build can write the map during the read. A concurrent map read and write is a fatal Go runtime error, so this can crash the process.

Fix: take b.cacheMu.RLock() in TotalDocs, as GetIndex does.

verification.reason: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock (bleve.go:146), while BuildIndex writes it under cacheMu (bleve.go:137-139). Collect (bleve_index_metrics.go:96) and the new init log call (search.go:216, which runs after the watch goroutine starts) can both read the map during a build triggered by a watch event.

findings.title: Same-key index builds can now run concurrently
findings.body:
Before the diff, BuildIndex held cacheMu for the whole build, so builds could not overlap. Now only the cache write is locked (bleve.go:137-139). getOrCreateIndex checks GetIndex and then builds without any lock (search.go:292-305), so a Search request and a watch event for the same new key can both reach BuildIndex.

For file-based indexes both calls run bleve.New on the same directory (bleve.go:97-98). For memory indexes, the later build replaces cache[key] while the earlier index may still receive watch-event writes, and those writes would then be missing from the cached index.

The check-then-build race predates the diff; the lock only serialized it. Is overlapping same-key builds intended, and what does bleve.New do when the directory already exists? I did not confirm the bleve behaviour.

verification.reason: BuildIndex now takes cacheMu only around the map write, so two getOrCreateIndex callers that both see nil (search.go:292-298) build the same key at the same time instead of one after the other. The duplicate-build and overwrite outcomes were already possible before the change, because the check-then-build race existed then too; the change only removes the serialization.

findings.title: Constructing a resource server now runs the full init synchronously
findings.body:
NewResourceServer now calls s.Init (server.go:258). Init runs the lifecycle Init (DB init and ping), builds a search index for every namespace (search.go:186-193) and starts the watchers. Before, all of this ran on the first RPC. A search init error now fails construction (server.go:259-262) instead of failing each RPC.

Callers of NewResourceServer include pkg/storage/unified/sql/server.go:77, pkg/storage/unified/client.go:67, pkg/storage/unified/apistore/restoptions.go:52 and 87, and pkg/registry/apis/dashboard/legacy_storage.go:28. Startup of each of these now waits for index builds. The PR body does not say this is intended. Is eager init the intended behaviour for every caller?

verification.reason: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init synchronously (server.go:258). That runs lifecycle init, builds every index and starts the watcher, and an error now fails construction for all listed callers, e.g. sql/service.go:113 inside the dskit start function.

findings.title: Postgres run of the storage-server integration test is now skipped
findings.body:
The new skip (module_server_test.go:36-38) turns off the only postgres run of TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer. The reason "Works locally" has no linked issue, and the TODO has no owner.

This diff changes storage-server construction (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258), which this test exercises. Is the postgres failure the same eager-init behaviour? If so, the skip hides a regression rather than a flaky test.

verification.reason: The diff adds an unconditional skip for postgres (module_server_test.go:36-38). The only reason given is 'Works locally', with no linked issue, and the change to storage-server construction is in the same diff, so coverage is lost.

findings.title: init goroutines write a shared counter and the outer err
findings.body:
Inside group.Go, totalBatchesIndexed++ (search.go:189) and the assignment _, _, err = s.build(...) (search.go:190) write variables shared by all goroutines with no synchronization. group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers) lets them run in parallel. The race predates the diff, but the narrowed BuildIndex lock (bleve.go:137-139) now lets the builds overlap. The race detector flags this, and the namespaced_indexed count reported at search.go:199 can be wrong.

Fix: declare err inside the closure and use an atomic counter, or drop the counter.
findings.originReason: The base has the same unsynchronized increment and err assignment in the goroutine, outside the BuildIndex lock.

verification.reason: totalBatchesIndexed++ and the outer err are written from several errgroup goroutines with no synchronization (search.go:189-190). Both writes happen outside BuildIndex, so the old lock never protected them; the same code is in the base.

contracts.before_after: Before: Init ran once, lazily, on the first RPC, and each RPC returned its error (the gate was removed from Create at 451). After: Init runs inside the constructor; a failure returns nil, err (server.go:259-262).
contracts.visible_effect: Startup blocks on DB init and the full search index build. A failed init stops construction instead of failing requests.
contracts.failure_mode: The error is returned to the caller of NewResourceServer; pkg/storage/unified/sql/server.go:77-80 propagates it. Init logs the error at server.go:314 and the constructor logs it again at server.go:260.

contracts.action: RPCs no longer call Init, so they are no longer gated after Stop
contracts.before_after: Before: after Stop set initErr, every RPC returned that error from Init. After: the RPCs run against the backend, and IsHealthy returns the diagnostics result (server.go:934-935).
contracts.visible_effect: Writes after Stop succeed, and health checks keep reporting healthy during shutdown.
contracts.failure_mode: A write is acknowledged but never indexed: backend Stop cancels the poller (backend.go:119-121, 575-578) and search only consumes WatchWriteEvents (search.go:203-213). Watchers are also cut off, because s.cancel() stops the broadcaster context.

contracts.before_after: Before: TotalDocs was only called from the metrics scrape. After: it is also called in init, after the watch goroutine has started (search.go:207-213).
contracts.failure_mode: TotalDocs reads b.cache without cacheMu while BuildIndex can write it from the watch goroutine (bleve.go:137-139, 144-154), a possible concurrent map read and write.

contracts.action: BuildIndex holds cacheMu only around the cache write
contracts.before_after: Before: the whole BuildIndex ran under cacheMu, so builds were serialized. After: only the map write is locked, so builds can overlap. getOrCreateIndex checks GetIndex and then builds with no lock (search.go:292-305).
contracts.visible_effect: Init and request-time builds can run in parallel.
contracts.failure_mode: Two builds for the same key can run at once. For file-based indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory (bleve.go:97-98). For memory indexes the later build replaces the cached index while the earlier one may still receive watch writes.
contracts.open_question: Can two BuildIndex calls for the same key overlap in practice, and what does bleve.New do when the index directory already exists?

contracts.action: initWatcher now runs after search init
contracts.before_after: Before: initWatcher ran before search init. After: it runs after, only if search init succeeded.
contracts.failure_mode: If search init fails, the broadcaster is never created, but construction fails too (server.go:258-262), so no server is handed out.

contracts.action: GetResourceStats uses the span context for its database work
contracts.before_after: Before: WithTx received the caller's ctx. After: it receives the span context, which has the same cancellation and deadline. The create path already uses this pattern.

summary: Reviewed the five files in this part. Main problems: (1) the Init gate removed from the RPCs means calls after Stop() are no longer rejected, so writes can be acknowledged without being indexed and health keeps reporting healthy during shutdown; (2) TotalDocs reads the bleve cache without the lock that the diff now uses for writes, which can crash the process under concurrent metrics scrapes or the new startup log; (3) narrowing the BuildIndex lock lets same-key builds overlap (question, low confidence); (4) constructing a server now blocks on the full index build, which the PR body does not mention; (5) the postgres run of the storage-server integration test is skipped without a linked issue; (6) the init goroutines write shared variables without synchronization (predates the diff). The sql/backend.go context change is safe. Note: docs/adr does not exist in this snapshot, so the ADR check could not be run against it.
